clue.text: Eccentric chap, one working in programming, including games principally

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece sits within the other
principally means first and foremost, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: a programmer writes code
the initial letter of the word

explanation.surface: A quirky programmer who spends much of the job making video games.
explanation.walkthrough: The G slips between the D and E of CODER to give CODGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A codger is an informal word for an old man, usually one thought of as odd or cantankerous.

clue.text: Alloy always only half finished

indicators.note: a job only half finished stops midway, so the second half of the word is dropped

blocks.note: a ten-letter synonym meaning without exception

explanation.surface: A metal mixture that never gets more than half made.
explanation.walkthrough: INVARIABLY has ten letters, so keeping the first five gives INVAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Invar is a nickel-iron alloy prized because it barely expands with heat, used in clocks and precision instruments.

clue.text: With Yard anticipating limits on policy, my friend and I will be waving goodbye

definitions.text: my friend and I will be waving goodbye

indicators.note: limits are boundaries, so only the outermost letters of the word are kept
to anticipate is to come before, so one piece goes ahead of the next

blocks.note: 'with' and 'and' both join one thing to another
Y is the standard abbreviation for yard
first and last letters of the word
taken as written, sitting between the limits

explanation.surface: Two friends at Scotland Yard are about to leave, waving goodbye once the policy limits arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' of 'my friend and I' does double duty, sitting inside P...Y. Andy Pandy was a BBC children's puppet show whose closing song was 'Andy is waving goodbye'.
explanation.definitionFit: Each episode ended with the puppet boy and his friends singing 'Time to go home', the boy waving goodbye to the young viewers.

clue.text: Dog track

blocks.note: first meaning: to dog someone is to tail them
second meaning: to track is to trail or pursue

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a greyhound racing venue, but both words are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to pursue or shadow someone closely, staying on their trail wherever they go.

clue.text: Pinter play involving three people: a woman and two men

blocks.note: Bet, short for Elizabeth, is a woman's name
two men's names, Ray and Al

explanation.surface: A Harold Pinter play with a cast of three: one woman and two men.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true: the 1978 play is a love triangle between a woman, her husband and his best friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayal is the title of Harold Pinter's 1978 drama about an adulterous affair, told in reverse chronological order.

clue.text: A person that really suits eimi, taking a stimulant drug

blocks.note: 'that's so me' is said of something that really suits the speaker, and eimi is the setter
a person on a drug is taking it
E is slang for ecstasy

explanation.surface: The setter eimi has found a person ideally suited to them, one who happens to be on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's name stands for ME, as 'this setter' would. 'So me' is the slang compliment for something that fits you perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone is a pronoun for an unspecified individual, which is exactly what an indefinite person is.

clue.text: Cockney's to give assistance carrying last serving of gefilte fish

indicators.note: Cockney speech drops the aitch at the start of words, so an initial H goes
the last serving is the final portion, so only the closing letter is kept
to carry something is to hold it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to help out is to give assistance
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Londoner offering to help by bringing the final portion of gefilte fish, a Jewish dish of poached fish balls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gefilte fish' reads as one dish, but only 'fish' is the definition. Dropping the H gives 'ELP OUT, and the E goes in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The eelpout is a real species, an elongated eel-like bottom-dwelling sea fish, so it is an example of a fish.

clue.text: No matter who is in first class going around 26

indicators.note: to go around something is to surround it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: A1 means first class, spelt out as A ONE
the answer to 26 is New York, abbreviated NY

explanation.surface: Whoever travels first class on a trip round New York.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is the old shipping register's top grade, hence first class. The 26 cross-reference points to NEW YORK, shortened to its usual NY.
explanation.definitionFit: 'No matter who' means any person at all, the indefinite pronoun used when the identity is unimportant.

clue.text: Girl getting particular shade of brown somewhere in Ireland

blocks.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
a particular is a respect or detail, as in 'in every way' and 'in every particular'
bay is a reddish-brown, the colour of a bay horse

explanation.surface: A girl acquires a specific brown tan while holidaying somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Particular' looks like an adjective qualifying the shade, but it is a noun meaning a respect or point.
explanation.definitionFit: Galway Bay is a large inlet of the Atlantic on Ireland's west coast, so it is an Irish location.

clue.text: Mathematician from Swiss city university flipping unwell

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: Bern is the Swiss capital
OU is the Open University, the UK's distance-learning university
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A mathematician from a Swiss university city who is feeling flipping awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British intensifier, but it is the turnaround signal. The university here is the Open University, not the usual U or UNI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bernoullis were a Swiss family of eminent mathematicians, notably Jacob, Johann and Daniel, from Basel.

clue.text: Reign changing hands, which has some attraction

indicators.note: the hands are right and left, so each R becomes L and each L becomes R

blocks.note: to reign is to rule

explanation.surface: A reign passing to a new holder, which has a certain appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing hands' usually means changing owner; here R (right) and L (left) swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: A lure is something that tempts or entices, a bait or enticement drawing people towards it.

clue.text: Sing "The King is in the altogether" cryptically

blocks.note: CR, Carolus Rex, is King Charles's royal cipher
someone in the altogether has nothing on, read as O (nothing) + ON

explanation.surface: A song lyric about a naked monarch, the Emperor's New Clothes set to music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the altogether' is a British idiom for naked; 'cryptically' tells you to take it as 'nothing on'. The King could be Elvis, but here he is Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: To croon is to sing softly and sentimentally, in the low smooth style of Bing Crosby.

clue.text: Lady in 26 with method to find theatre district

blocks.note: broad is American slang for a woman, the kind of word heard in New York
a way is a method

explanation.surface: A woman in New York has a technique for locating the theatres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In 26' qualifies the lady: broad is a New York kind of word for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadway is the Manhattan avenue whose surrounding blocks hold New York's major commercial theatres.

clue.text: A fight following one change of policy

blocks.note: taken as written
a bout is a fight, as in boxing
F is the abbreviation for following, as in 'p. 12f'
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A row breaking out after a government U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like it sets the order of pieces, but it supplies the F of reference books.
explanation.definitionFit: An about-face is literally a military turn to face the opposite way, figuratively a complete reversal of stance.

clue.text: Clothes billowed unfortunately revealing vital components

indicators.note: something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters fall out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gust of wind lifts someone's clothes and exposes their private parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifteen letters of the two words rearrange exactly; 'vital components' are vital to life, not intimate anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Leucocytes are an essential part of the blood, fighting infection, so they are components we cannot live without.

clue.text: Little Jack briefly hugging Philip in dance

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, so the final letter is dropped
to hug is to wrap your arms round, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: Little Jack Horner is the nursery-rhyme boy who sat in a corner eating pie
Pip is a short form of Philip, as with the hero of Great Expectations

explanation.surface: A small boy called Jack gives Philip a quick cuddle on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Jack' looks like a description of a small boy, but it is the nursery-rhyme character, and 'briefly' trims his surname by its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The hornpipe is a lively solo dance traditionally associated with sailors.

clue.text: A flower opening?

blocks.note: surface reading: a bloom unfurling its petals
setter's reading: something that flows, a river, and the place where it opens out into the sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword's favourite trick: read it as flow-er, one that flows, meaning a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An estuary is the wide tidal mouth where a river widens and meets the sea, its opening.

clue.text: Call about large drink

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
a double is a large measure of spirits

explanation.surface: Phoning someone about having a big drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call' is not a phone call but a bid in the card game bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, redouble is a call made after an opponent doubles, increasing the scoring stakes again.

clue.text: West caught up in cricket review system fantasies

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
something caught is held fast, so one piece is trapped inside the other

blocks.note: Mae West was the Hollywood actress and wisecracker
DRS is the Decision Review System used to check umpires' calls in cricket

explanation.surface: Batsmen from the West Indies daydreaming about an umpire review going their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' is not a direction but Mae West; turned round she sits inside DRS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreams are imaginings or wishful fantasies, things hoped for that may never come true.

clue.text: Somewhat nautical area of 26

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only a part of the following words is used

blocks.note: the letters run from the second to the sixth of this word

explanation.surface: A part of New York with a slightly maritime feel.
explanation.walkthrough: The 26 cross-reference is NEW YORK, here the state, not the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Utica is a city in central New York State, on the Mohawk River, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Note hidden in singer's toast

indicators.note: a thing tucked inside something else is held within it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: E is a musical note
Cher is the American pop singer, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A message tucked away in a singer's speech at a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: The note is not a written message but a musical letter, which slips into CHER'S after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Cheers!' is the word said when raising glasses to drink someone's health, a toast.

clue.text: Overstimulated PR person

blocks.note: first meaning: excitable and over-energetic
second meaning: one who promotes or puffs things up

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the setter's coinage: someone who hypes, as a publicist does.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means wildly overexcited; the noun is an agent word for someone who generates publicity hype.

clue.text: An opening perhaps education provides

indicators.note: to provide is to supply from within, so the words themselves supply the letters

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Schooling may give you a start in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' looks like it qualifies the definition, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a vaulted semicircular recess in a church wall, a kind of architectural niche or alcove.

clue.text: Note altered reality in this story

indicators.note: something altered has been changed, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: fa is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale
taken as written

explanation.surface: A story in which the truth has been changed and written down.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue nods to the answer: reality is altered in a fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy tale is a children's story of magic and make-believe, a narrative where real life is transformed.

clue.text: Stone fruit left out next to frozen water

indicators.note: something put out is excluded or omitted, so that letter is removed
next to means beside, so the pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: a plum is a stone fruit
L is the abbreviation for left
ice is frozen water

explanation.surface: A plum or cherry forgotten beside some ice cubes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone fruit' looks like one phrase for a plum, but 'Stone' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is a light porous volcanic rock, used for scrubbing hard skin, so it is a kind of stone.

clue.text: City-state

blocks.note: first meaning: the largest city in the United States
second meaning: the US state containing that city

explanation.walkthrough: 'City-state' suggests an ancient polis like Athens or a modern one like Singapore; the hyphen hides two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name belongs both to the metropolis on the Hudson and to the American state it sits in.
